question.:question/problem:
Consider the following first-order linear ODE for the function $y = y(x)$:
$\frac{dy}{dx}-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\cdot y=\cos{\left(x \right)}$
Write the equation in the form $\frac{d}{dx}(yI(x)) = I(x)Q(x)$, where $I(x)$ is an integrating factor.
question.:question/worked-solution:
This equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+P(x)y=Q(x)
$$

with $P(x)=- \frac{2}{3}$ and $Q(x)=\cos{\left(x \right)}.$ We proceed to find an integrating factor $I(x)$ using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & =e^{\int P(x)\,dx} \\  & =e^{\int \left(- \frac{2}{3}\right)\,dx} \\  & =e^{- \frac{2 x}{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply our differential equation through by $I(x)=e^{- \frac{2 x}{3}}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(e^{- \frac{2 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \left(\frac{dy}{dx}-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\cdot y\right) & =\left(e^{- \frac{2 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \left(\cos{\left(x \right)}\right) \\ \left(e^{- \frac{2 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \frac{dy}{dx}-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\cdot \left(e^{- \frac{2 x}{3}}\right)\cdot y & =\left(e^{- \frac{2 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \left(\cos{\left(x \right)}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the left hand side as $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y\cdot I(x)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dx}\left(y\cdot \left(e^{- \frac{2 x}{3}}\right)\right) & =\left(e^{- \frac{2 x}{3}}\right)\cdot \left(\cos{\left(x \right)}\right)\end{aligned}
$$
